@graph.headline: Five Articles Every Custom Home Builder Blog Needs
@graph.description: Build a useful custom home builder blog with five article types that answer buyer questions, demonstrate expertise, support sales, and create clear next steps.

mainEntity.name: What articles should a custom home builder blog publish first?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start with five: how the custom home process works, what affects the investment, how to choose the right builder, a project story with the decisions left in, and what to do before the first consultation.

mainEntity.name: What should we prepare before the first conversation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bring the reason you want to build, preferred markets or land status, essential needs versus flexible ideas, timing constraints, and a working sense of investment. Uncertainty is normal. The conversation is meant to help, not to grade homework.

mainEntity.name: Do we need land or plans already?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always. A useful process article should say whether land, plans, or a separate architect are required before a productive first conversation, and what the team can review if those pieces are still open.
The article should name who guides design: the builder, the homeowner, an architect, or a coordinated team. The point is to show how decisions are made, not to pretend every project is identical.

mainEntity.name: How do we know whether our goals and investment align?

acceptedAnswer.text: Alignment becomes clearer when site conditions, design complexity, selections, and local requirements are discussed against a realistic planning horizon. An early number is not a construction-ready price.

mainEntity.name: What happens after we decide to move forward?

acceptedAnswer.text: A clear process article explains the next owned steps: engagement, design or feasibility work, scope alignment, selections, construction communication, and handoff. If the sales page and the real process disagree, fix the gap before publishing.
